info.title: Arbitron API
info.description:
Funding rates, executable cross-venue spreads and the listings calendar across the perpetual futures venues Arbitron tracks. Read-only JSON over HTTPS. API and MCP access are part of every Arbitron plan: see [the plans](https://arbitron.app/developers#plans).

## Authentication

Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer arb_live_...` (the `X-Api-Key` header is accepted too). Create one at https://arbitron.app/settings/api; it is shown once. MCP clients can sign in with an Arbitron account through OAuth 2.1 instead of a key.

## Rate limits

Each key has a minute window and a month window, sized by its plan. Both are advertised on every response in the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` fields, so a client can pace itself and never see a `429`. For example:

```http
RateLimit-Policy: "minute";q=120;w=60, "month";q=100000;w=2592000
RateLimit: "minute";r=118;t=41, "month";r=87500;t=1209600
```

`q` is the quota for the window, `w` its length in seconds, `r` the requests left and `t` the seconds until it resets.

- A spent window answers `429` with `Retry-After` in seconds and a problem body naming the window.
- The month resets on the 1st at 00:00 UTC. Quotas are hard caps; nothing is ever billed as overage.
- One request is one request: history, spreads and funding cost the same, and an MCP tool call counts like a REST call.

## Caching

Every data response carries an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged body answers `304`, which is refunded on both windows. `Cache-Control` is `private, max-age=15` on live data and `max-age=300` on delayed data, matching how often the snapshot behind it moves.

## Errors

Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`): `type`, `title`, `status`, a `detail` that says what to change, the request id as `instance`, a stable `code`, and `suggestions` where a close match exists. `type` is `https://arbitron.app/developers/errors#<code>`, and every code is explained at [https://arbitron.app/developers/errors](https://arbitron.app/developers/errors).

## Versioning

`/api/v1` is the contract. Fields, endpoints, enum values and optional parameters are added without a version change. Removing or renaming anything, changing a type or changing a default is v2, and v1 keeps working for twelve months after v2 ships. A deprecated endpoint or field announces itself with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers and a `Link` to the changelog entry that names the replacement. The MCP server follows the same version, and tool names never change within a major version.

### Changelog

- **2026-09-20** v1 published: funding, funding history, spreads, listings, exchanges, coins and usage. MCP server with eight tools, key or OAuth.

get.summary: Current funding rate on every venue and symbol
get.description:
One row per perpetual contract on every venue Arbitron tracks, sorted by absolute rate. Rates are percent per settlement; `apr_pct` is the annualised carry net of costs.

- Filter by coin, venue, signed or absolute rate bounds, APR, 7d/30d sums, settlement interval, contract type, volume and time to the next settlement.
- Sort by any of them with `sort`.
- Page with `cursor`.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: One ticker or a comma-separated list, e.g. `BTC,ETH`. Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: exchange
parameters.description: Keep rows on these venues. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: exclude_exchange
parameters.description: Drop rows on these venues. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: min_rate_pct
parameters.description: Keep rows whose `rate_pct` is at least this (signed), e.g. `0.05` or `-0.01`.

parameters.name: max_rate_pct
parameters.description: Keep rows whose `rate_pct` is at most this (signed), e.g. `-0.01` for negative funding only.

parameters.name: min_abs_rate_pct
parameters.description: Keep rows whose `|rate_pct|` is at least this, e.g. `0.05`.

parameters.name: max_abs_rate_pct
parameters.description: Keep rows whose `|rate_pct|` is at most this.

parameters.name: min_apr_pct
parameters.description: Keep rows whose `apr_pct` is at least this (signed). Rows without an APR are dropped.

parameters.name: max_apr_pct

parameters.description: Keep rows settling on these intervals, comma-separated, e.g. `1` or `4,8`.

get.summary: Funding history, daily or per settlement
get.description:
Two resolutions:

- `resolution=1d`: one annualised APR point per day for each venue quoting the coin, up to 180 days.
- `resolution=settlement`: every settlement print for one venue, up to 92 days per call.

Window by `from`/`to` or `days`. `order=desc` with `limit` reads the last N points. How far back you may reach depends on the plan.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Ticker, e.g. `BTC`.

parameters.name: exchange
parameters.description: Venues to include; a list for `1d`, exactly one for `settlement`. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: exclude_exchange
parameters.description: Venues to leave out (`1d`). One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: `1d` (default) or `settlement`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 8601 UTC. Default: 30 days before `to` (`1d`) or 7 days (`settlement`).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 8601 UTC. Default: now.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Shortcut for `from`: this many days before `to`, 1 to 180. Ignored when `from` is given.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `asc` (default, oldest first) or `desc` (newest first).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Points per series at most, 1 to 5000, taken after ordering: `order=desc&limit=10` is the last ten.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated row fields to keep, e.g. `exchange,coin,rate_pct`; the others are dropped from every row. Unknown names are a 400 that lists the fields.

get.description:
The spread between two venues' perpetuals on the same coin right now, one row per venue pair and symbol, from the engine's last print (seconds old). `spread_pct` is the better of the two entry directions and `direction` says which; both are given, with the bid and ask on each leg.

On the Demo plan the print arrives 15 minutes late, and the five widest spreads of every venue (on either leg) are withheld whatever the filter. `meta.withheld` is the number withheld from the whole snapshot, the same whatever the filter, and the cursor stops after 100 rows.

For how often a spread paid over a window, use `/spreads/backtest`.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: One ticker or a comma-separated list, e.g. `BTC,ETH`. Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: exchange
parameters.description: Keep pairs with these venues. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: exchange_match
parameters.description: `any` (default): either leg is in `exchange`. `all`: both legs are, i.e. spreads among the listed venues only.

parameters.name: exclude_exchange
parameters.description: Drop pairs with any of these venues on either leg. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: min_spread_pct
parameters.description: Keep pairs whose `spread_pct` is at least this many percent, e.g. `0.3`.

parameters.name: max_spread_pct
parameters.description: Keep pairs whose `spread_pct` is at most this many percent, e.g. `5` to drop dead markets.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: `long_a_short_b` or `short_a_long_b`: keep pairs whose better side is that one. Default: both.

parameters.name: min_volume_usdt
parameters.description: Keep pairs where BOTH legs' 24h volume is at least this many USDT, e.g. `500000`.

parameters.name: min_strength
parameters.description: Keep pairs whose `strength` is at least this, 0 to 5.

parameters.name: max_age_seconds
parameters.description: Keep pairs printed within this many seconds of `meta.as_of`, 1 to 120.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `spread_desc` (default), `spread_asc`, `volume_desc`, `volume_asc`, `strength_desc`, `updated_desc`, `coin_asc`. Volume is the smaller leg's.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows per page, 1 to 500 (Demo: 50). Default 100.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `meta.next_cursor` from the previous page.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated row fields to keep, e.g. `exchange,coin,rate_pct`; the others are dropped from every row. Unknown names are a 400 that lists the fields.

get.description:
The public scanner's ranked spreads, priced against real order-book depth for an order of `size_usd` over the scan window. `est_profit_pct` is per round trip after fees; `cycles` counts how often the spread opened and closed. `strategy_url` opens a new strategy on the pair in the terminal, coin and both venues filled in.

A backtest, not the live print: use `/spreads` for what the spread is right now. The Demo plan withholds the five best rows of every venue (on either leg) whatever the filter. `withheld_top` is the number withheld from the whole snapshot, the same whatever the filter, and the cursor stops after 100 rows. Paid plans see every row.

parameters.name: size_usd
parameters.description: Order size the depth is priced at: `25`, `100` or `500`. Default `100`.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: One ticker or a comma-separated list, e.g. `BTC,ETH`. Case-insensitive.

parameters.name: exchange

parameters.name: exclude_exchange
parameters.description: Drop spreads with any of these venues on either leg. One venue or a comma-separated list, spelled as `/exchanges` spells it, e.g. `Binance,Bybit`.

parameters.name: min_profit_pct
parameters.description: Keep spreads whose `est_profit_pct` is at least this.

parameters.name: max_profit_pct
parameters.description: Keep spreads whose `est_profit_pct` is at most this.

parameters.name: min_avg_profit_pct
parameters.description: Keep spreads whose `avg_profit_pct` is at least this.

parameters.name: min_cycles
parameters.description: Keep spreads that opened and closed at least this many times over the window.

parameters.name: min_confidence
parameters.description: Keep spreads whose `confidence` is at least this, 0 to 100.

parameters.name: min_volume_usdt
parameters.description: Keep spreads where BOTH legs' 24h volume is at least this many USDT.

parameters.name: active_within_hours
parameters.description: Keep spreads whose last cycle closed within this many hours, 1 to 720.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `profit_desc` (default), `profit_asc`, `avg_profit_desc`, `cycles_desc`, `confidence_desc`, `volume_desc`, `spread_range_desc`, `last_cycle_desc`, `coin_asc`.

Every venue the API serves, with tracked instrument counts, maximum leverage, the default taker fee and links to its contract specs and funding pages. Filter by name, tradability or spot; sort by instruments, fee or leverage.

Any valid key can call it; no scope is needed.

parameters.description: `true` keeps venues with a spot market, `false` the rest. Default: all.

get.description:
Ticker lookup: `q` matches the start of a ticker, or anywhere in it with `match=contains`. Each coin carries the venues quoting it and its 24h perpetual volume; filter by venue, venue count or volume.

Any valid key can call it; no scope is needed.

parameters.description: Text to match against the ticker, e.g. `PE` matches PEPE and PENDLE.

parameters.name: match
parameters.description: `prefix` (default): `q` is the start of the ticker. `contains`: `q` appears anywhere, so `PEPE` also finds 1000PEPE.

parameters.name: exchange

parameters.name: exchange_match
parameters.description: `any` (default): quoted on at least one of `exchange`. `all`: quoted on every one of them.

parameters.name: min_venues
parameters.description: Keep coins quoted on at least this many venues, 1 to 64.

parameters.name: min_volume_usdt
parameters.description: Keep coins whose 24h perpetual volume across venues is at least this many USDT.

get.description:
One row per card: coin, the two exchanges and accounts, mode (`classic` or `one_leg`), status (`running`, `open`, `error`, `closed`), the open and close spread thresholds in percent, order size and unit, filled orders against the maximum, leverage, net PnL over the card's life, this session and today, the last fill and any error reason.

Cards are addressed by `card_ref`, a handle that means something only to this account. `meta.total` counts every card that matched.

get.description:
Executed trades over a window of up to 31 days (default: the last 7), grouped by card: per card the net PnL, profit percent on capital, fees, funding and fills, and the newest paired trades with both legs, the venue's order id and any unwind. Window totals cover every trade.

At most 300 pairs are listed in one answer across all cards; `pairs_truncated` says when more exist. For daily or monthly totals over longer periods use `/me/pnl`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Window start, ISO 8601 UTC. Default: 7 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to

get.description: Every connected exchange account: equity (wallet plus unrealized PnL), unrealized PnL, the maintenance margin as a percent of equity where the venue reports it (100 = liquidation), each currency worth at least 1 USD (smaller balances summed into `dust_usd`), and every open position. Each account carries its own `as_of`.

How each exchange account's equity moved over the last `days` (1 to 180, default 30): start and end equity, the change, the closing equity of each UTC day, and the newest 100 deposits, withdrawals, transfers, liquidations and bonuses.

ApiKey.description: Your API key as a bearer token. The X-Api-Key header is accepted too.

tags.name: Reference data
tags.description: The venues, the coins and the listings calendar: what exists, what it is called, and what is about to be listed or delisted. Use the names these return to fill the `exchange` and `coin` parameters everywhere else.

tags.name: Funding
tags.description: Funding rates on every perpetual contract, one coin across venues, and history by day or by settlement. Rates are percent per settlement; `apr_pct` is annualised.

tags.name: Spreads
tags.description: Cross-venue spreads on the same coin: the live print from the spread engine, and the scanner's backtest priced against order-book depth.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Your own account: cards, trades, PnL, balances and positions, connected exchange accounts, leaderboard place and plan. Needs a key with the `account:read` scope, which is never granted by default. Cards are addressed by `card_ref`; exchange keys and anything about Arbitron's servers are never returned.

tags.name: Platform
tags.description: Discovery and your key's usage. Authentication, rate limits, caching, errors and versioning are covered in the introduction above.
